scope: Proposition G.4 (High-scale pin) of the manuscript “Uniform Cartier sections for Fano type contractions” (preprints/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 066 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d97ba60373419ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 87. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a high stage with pre-pinning slice, working valuation w, baseline height B, scale L, and s selected values as above. After passage to a subsequence, finitely many invariant tests of cost O(L) can be added with the following properties. (i) The resulting slice contains a centred valuation. The added tests are exact on that slice, all old tests and proportionalities remain in force, and the accumulated positive symbols remain algebraically independent at the exact minimizer and working valuation in (iii) below. (ii) The selected values either vanish or lie on a single rational line. In the line case their proportions have the bounds (G.3), with L− = L. An old anchor remains the anchor; if a new anchor is chosen, its scale is L1 = L. (iii) The baseline height is retained unless an anchor is first chosen, in which case it may change to the rational height (G.5). It satisfies (G.4) on the new actual slice. At its exact minimizer v′, and at an arbitrarily close rank refinement w′, the anchor, when present, satisfies |v′(Y + 0 )|, |w′(Y + 0 )| ≥ cL1. Both valuations dominate a fixed positive multiple of w on every regular function. In particular, w′ ≥ cw. Consequently (I1)–(I5) hold with L− = L. The next-scale assertions (H1)–(H2) are not assumed in constructing the pin or its rank refinement.
